utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, good afternoon, everyone. This is the continued initial appearance in the case of Beara. What I propose to do initially is to take the appearances for counsel. The Prosecution first of all, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: May it please, Your Honour. I appear on behalf of the Prosecutor. My name is Cayley, I appear with my colleagues Ms. Caroline Davidson and Ms. Janet Stewart.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cayley. Ms. Featherstone, what I note I didn't do is have the case called. Is that vital to the process? I note I omitted to have the case formally called, so I'll invite the Registrar to do that before calling on the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is Case Number IT-02-58-I, the Prosecutor versus Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And now the appearance for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Gregor Guy-Smith appearing on behalf of Mr. Beara for the proceedings being held today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And I rightly noted you appeared on the previous occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I'm addressing myself now directly to the accused, Mr. Beara. Mr. Beara, can you hear me and understand what I am saying?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Could you please give your name formally for the record.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ljubisa Beara.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Your date of birth, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The 14th of July, 1939.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Guy-Smith, today should have been the occasion on which pleas were tendered by Mr. Beara. Can you tell me whether you are in a position to deal with that.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: Your Honour, it was contemplated that pleas would be entered today by counsel who ultimately will be representing Mr. Beara in this matter, who my understanding is Mr. John Ostojic. However, probably because of circumstances outside of his control, he was not able to be present today. I'm sure if you recognise he's a much larger man than I, and I am not in a position, not only because of his size but also because of his status with Mr. Beara, to at this point enter a plea or have Mr. Beara enter a plea for purposes of today's proceedings. And I would request that the matter be adjourned. My application is for the matter be adjourned for I believe only two days, at which point Mr. Ostojic will be present and he will be able to address those issues that are germane to the Court's consideration. I believe we are still within the time constraints that allow for him to enter his plea in an appropriate period of time without offending any jurisdictional concerns.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Now, Mr. Cayley, do you have any comment on that first of all.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Not on that issue, no. Mr. Guy-Smith and I have discussed and it seems the correct course to take.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Is there anything else you would like to raise?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: This is one issue you should know about before the plea is tendered on Thursday, and that it is the intention of the Office of the Prosecutor to file an amended indictment in this case within two weeks of today. I realise, in a sense, it's not entirely the best way of doing things since he will be entering pleas on the old indictment, but that -- do you want me to go into the background of why it's being amended now or do you think that's best left until Thursday? I can explain it to you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Are there any circumstances in which you envisage it might not be appropriate to take the pleas on Thursday?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Well, I think -- I mean, it's been pointed out to me that the rules demand that he enter pleas by Thursday. I think it's Rule 62 requires that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: If that is the case, then is there any point in going into the matter at all and is it not a matter which should simply be dealt with by a motion when the appropriate amended indictment is filed?

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: That's a perfect solution, Your Honour. I just wanted the courtesy of actually telling you so that you weren't surprised when he entered pleas and we had a new indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: I appreciate that. But perhaps for the avoidance of any doubt whatsoever you should give consideration between now and Thursday to the question whether there is any alternative to simply taking the pleas on this indictment and leaving the matter you now raise until it is filed.

utterances.speaker: MR. CAYLEY
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Well, in these circumstances, what I shall do is further adjourn this initial appearance until Thursday of this week, I understand, in Courtroom II at 3 p.m.
